newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Snacks firm Armato makes poor JSE debut.
newsitem.headline: Snacks firm Armato makes poor JSE debut.

text.p: Armato Corporation Ltd made a weak debut on the Johannesburg Stock Exchange on Tuesday hit by hectic interest in the futures close-out and poor market sentiment, dealers said.
The December futures close-out was at 1000 GMT and pushed the cash market lower, dealers said.
"They haven't got a good listing. Today was a bad day to list. We had the futures close-out and most guys played futures," one dealer said.
Armato, through its wholly owned subsidiary Collondale Consumer Products, is a manufacturer and distributor of snack foods and confectionery and a miller of maize.
Its shares opened at 300 cents and touched a low of 238 cents before settling at 270 cents by 1320 GMT. Volumes were slim, with 54,400 shares traded valued at 140,000 rand.
Buyers and sellers were in a tug-of-war before the close-out but now buyers were holding on to their money, dealers said.
Dealers said if market sentiment turned during the next few days interest in the stock could be rekindled.
